parties:
Nawab Khaja Habibullah Askari & others ------ Petitioners 
Vs
Bangladesh and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Amin J: This Rule has been obtained upon an application filed under Article 102(2)(a)(ii) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh calling upon the respondents Nos.1-5 to show cause as to why they should not be directed to release the Estate of late Nawab of Dhaka Khaja Salimullah Bahadur from the custody of Court of Wards in favour of the petitioners (4 in all) and respondent Nos. 6-8, 10-34, 36-39 and 41-47. 

 2. In support of the prayer of having the properties, as claimed to have been of late Nowab of Dhaka Khaja Salimullah, released from the custody of Court of Wards petitioners have stated, inter alia, that said Nowab mortgaged some properties to Raja Sreenath Roy and others of Bhaggapur and also to Raja Sreenath Roy; that the mortgage suit Nos. 12 of 1907 and 16 of 1907 were instituted by the mortgagees in the Court of First Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and they obtained decree therein; that the Nowab having found himself in a precarious financial predicament to satisfy the mortgage decrees applied for a loan of Taka 14 lakh to the Government of India, that the Secretary of State for India considered the application of the Nawab in council and communicated Government of India's decision to grant loan against the security of the movable and immovable properties of Nowab, that a mortgage deed was drawn and executed on 6th August, 1908 between the Court of Wards 1st Part and the Nowab in the second part and the Secretary of State for India in the third part; that by the aforesaid mortgage deed movable and immovable properties described in the schedule to the mortgage deed were mortgaged for satisfaction of debt of Taka 14 lakh out of which Taka 3,11,500 was paid by the Collector of Dhaka as purchase money together with incidental cost for repayment and purchase of mortgage decrees of Raja Sreenath Roy and others and adjusted, as such, against the said loan; that mortgage deed provided for repayment of debt with interest at the stipulated rate within 30 years by the Court of Wards. It was further stipulated in the mortgage deed, that neither the said ward nor his heirs, successors, executors, administrator and assigns shall be able to take back any of the property mortgaged from the custody of the Court of Wards as long as the whole amount of mortgaged money is not repaid; that 30 years period expired on 6-7-1938 and thereafter, another 57 years passed from August, 1938 but the property is still retained by the Court of Wards. It has been alleged that the Court of Wards did not furnish any statement of accounts of the repayment of debt either to the Nawab or to any of his heirs or successors and, as such, the petitioners and the respondent Nos. 6-8, 10-34, 36-39 and 41-47 are quite in the dark about the matter of repayment of loan. It has been contended by the petitioners that they have reasonable cause to believe that out of the income of the mortgage property the loan of Taka 14 lakh had already been paid and the Court of Wards has been arbitrarily and illegally continuing the possession of the property mortgaged by the mortgage deed dated 6th August, 1908. 

 3. Respondent Nos. 2 and 5—The Chairman, Land Reform Board and the Chief Manager of Court of Wards—respectively have entered appearances and have filed affidavit-in-opposition. These respondents upon denying the correctness of the material averments made in the writ petition have stated, inter alia, that the title i.e. Nowab, is not an inheritable one and that the claim of the petitioners as of being Nawab is unfounded and unsustainable one; that the claim of the petitioners that they and respondents Nos. 6-8, 10-34, 36-39 and 41-47, hereinafter referred to as said respondents, are the present sole exclusive heirs/successors is not correct, that neither the petitioners nor the said respondents had established their claim of inheritance and succession by any cogent evidence before the Court of Wards; that the petitioners nor the said respondents have filed any papers showing that they are the sole proprietor of the property which was placed under the management of the Court of Wards; that almost 50% of the wards of the original owner had left Bangladesh and that their whereabouts were not known, as such, their property has assumed the character of abandoned property and that vested in the Government as per provision of President's Order No.16 of 1972; that the said respondents have not filed any paper before the Court of Wards in support of their claim of being proprietor of the property managed by the Court of Wards, nor they have approached the Court of Wards seeking release of the property from the management thereof, that joint proprietorship has not been partitioned and, as such, the Court of Wards in the absence of determination of share of the petitioners as well as the said respondents and other proprietors of the property, in law, cannot release the property to the petitioners and the said respondents, that the petitioners have not made any statement as to how the mortgaged properties were redeemed and discharged from the mortgage debt, nor the petitioners have given any particulars and description of the property which was the subject matter of the mortgage; that it is not correct that the Court of Wards did not furnish any statement of account of repayment of debt either to the Nowab Khaja Salimullah Bahadur or to any of his heirs or successors, or it is correct that the petitioners and the said respondents were ignored about the matter; that the petitioners' contention of repayment of loan out of income of the mortgaged property and that even after repayment and disbursement of amount for which the property was mortgaged the Court of Wards was retaining the possession of the mortgaged property illegally is not correct; that it is not correct that before and after acquisition of rent receiving interest the officers of the Court of Wards in collusion with designing persons leased out, sold and otherwise disposed of various moveable and immovable mortgaged properties and mis-appropriated wholly or partly the proceeds of the mortgage property, that as there is ample provision under the Court of Wards Act for adjudication of the dispute of the kind as stated in the writ petition and that the petitioners having had not resorted to that forum the writ petition so filed is not maintainable; that it has not been established by any competent Court that the petitioners as well as the said respondents are the heirs and successors of Nowab of Dhaka Khaja Salimullah Bahadur and that they are the proprietors of the estate jointly or individually; that the matter of succession to the property of the estate by the petitioners and the said respondent being a disputed question and, as such, the Court of Wards cannot release the property until the dispute is resolved or determined by a competent Civil Court, that the petitioners ought to have reported to the Court of Wards for settlement of their claim in respect of the property in the light of the provision of the Court of Wards Act; that as there is conflicting claim amongst the wards and that joint proprietorship as has not been partitioned, the Court of Wards cannot release the property in favour of the petitioners and the said respondents. 

 7. Petitioners have filed the writ petition seeking release of the property which was placed under the management of the Court of Wards on the application of Nawab of Dhaka Khaja Salimullah Bahadur and that the said property was mortgaged jointly by the Nawab and the Court of Wards to the Secretary of State for India for repayment of the debt of Taka 14 lakh of the Nawab. It is the contention of the petitioners that the mortgage was made in 1908 for a period of 30 years as security towards the payment of Taka 14 lakh and that the said amount of Taka 14 lakh since 1908 and by the time till the date of filing of the writ petition has been repaid or satisfied and, as such, the petitioners and the said respondents being the heirs and successors in interest of the Nawab are entitled to have the property released from the management of Court of Wards. Against the aforesaid contention of the petitioners and the said respondents, the respondent Nos.2 and 5 have submitted that matter as to repayment or satisfaction of the debt needs adjudication on investigation of complicated facts and that that having not been done and that also no material having been placed in the writ petition in support of the claim of the petitioners that the mortgage debt has been satisfied, as such, relief that has been sought in the writ petition cannot be had to the petitioners or, in other words, writ petition cannot be maintained by the petitioners. Respondent Nos. 2 and 5 have also contended that part of the property that was placed under the management of the Court of Wards has become abandoned property and that in the absence of determination as to how much of the property has become abandoned property, petitioners' prayer for releasing the property to them that was placed under management of the Court of Wards by the mortgage deed of the year 1908 cannot be entertained.
